column1: # Every method of every API this server can reach, and the verdict on it.
# Phase 4's last deliverable in §16: the discovery documents diffed
# against what the client calls, so that the gap between the API and this
# server is a set of decisions rather than an accident.
# Columns, tab-separated: method, HTTP verb, path, verdict, reason.
# A verdict of `used` names the gapi.Client method that implements it;
# `out` gives the reason it is deliberately not used. `gates
# api-coverage` holds both directions and runs in `make check`; `gates
# api-diff` refetches the three discovery documents and reports what has
# changed, and reaches the network, so it is a target rather than a gate.
# Three parameters are deliberately unused and have no row of their own,
# because a row is per method:
#   useDomainAdminAccess  an administrator acting across an organisation
#                         is not what a per-user server is for.
#   supportsTeamDrives    the pre-2020 spelling of supportsAllDrives,
#   enforceSingleParent   Google documents it as deprecated and Drive
#                         gives a file one parent regardless.

column5: the listing carries every field a proposal has, so fetching one by id would be a second call for the same bytes
which third-party apps the account has installed says nothing about a file this server can act on
push needs a public HTTPS endpoint to receive callbacks, and a stdio server has none
there is nothing to stop: no channel is ever opened (see changes.watch)
client-side encryption needs a key service this server does not have and cannot stand in for
permissions.list returns every grant in full, so one grant by id is a second call for bytes already in hand
comments.list carries a thread's replies inline, so a reply is never fetched on its own
teamdrives is the pre-2020 name for drives and Google documents it as deprecated; drives.* is the same surface
